root_cause.text: In `bcmgenet_put_txcb`, the calculation of the tx_cb pointer was performed before decrementing the write pointer, causing the function to return the next open tx_cb (off by one) instead of the one being rewound for cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `tx_cb_ptr = ring->cbs; tx_cb_ptr += ring->write_ptr - ring->cb_ptr;` after the write pointer rewinding logic. The commit message explicitly states: "The write_ptr points to the next open tx_cb. We want to return the tx_cb that gets rewinded, so we must rewind the pointer first then return the tx_cb that it points to."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in bcmgenet_put_txcb by recalculating the CB pointer after updating the write pointer.
intent_record.what: Moved the calculation of tx_cb_ptr from before the update of ring->write_ptr to after it.
intent_record.how: The function now computes the pointer to the transmit control block (CB) using the decremented write pointer instead of the original value, ensuring it returns the correct CB slot after freeing.

candidates.rationale: The calculation of tx_cb_ptr uses the current write_ptr before it is decremented, causing the function to return the next open slot instead of the one being rewound for cleanup, leading to an off-by-one error.
